_comment: Unified tool schema registry. All tool types (NATIVE, MCP, API) defined here. Single source of truth for tool schemas across all services.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch readable content from a web page using the native web_fetch tool. The tool accepts an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL and retrieves readable page content using a direct HTTP request first, with the Jina AI Reader used as a fallback when necessary. When deep scraping is requested, the tool fetches the starter page and a limited number of unique same-domain links discovered directly on that page. It does not recursively crawl beyond those direct links. Deep scraping should be enabled when the user's query contains words or phrases that indicate a request for deeper or more detailed web content retrieval, including terms such as deep, detail, detailed, deepscrape, deepscrap, deep scrape, deep scraping, scrape deeply, scrape all, explore the page, explore the website, fetch related pages, fetch linked pages, or similar wording. In such cases, set deepScraping to true. If the query does not contain a deep-scraping indicator, use deepScraping=false unless the user explicitly requests otherwise. When deepScraping is enabled, maxLinks controls the maximum number of unique same-domain links discovered directly from the starter page that are fetched. The tool does not recursively crawl those discovered links.

deepScraping.description: Optional. If true, fetch the starter page and a limited number of unique direct same-domain links discovered from the starter page. Deep scraping is intended for queries containing indicators such as deep, detail, detailed, deepscrape, deepscrap, deep scrape, deep scraping, scrape deeply, scrape all, explore the page, explore the website, fetch related pages, or fetch linked pages.

maxLinks.description: Optional. Maximum number of unique direct same-domain links to fetch from the starter page when deep scraping is enabled.

maxCharacters.description: Optional. Maximum number of characters returned for each fetched page.

tools.name: extract
tools.description: Extract all available data from a supported source. Automatically detects the source type and selects the appropriate native extractor. Supports local files, HTTP/HTTPS URLs, S3 objects, and raw content. Supported file formats include PDF, DOCX, CSV, XLSX/XLS, images, HTML, JSON, XML, email, and Markdown.

source.description: The source to extract from. Pass exactly one key: {"url": "https://..."} for a web URL, {"path": "/path/to/file.pdf"} for a local file or "s3://bucket/key.pdf" for an S3 object (with sibling "credentials"), {"file": "/path/to/file"} as an alias for path, or {"content": "raw text or JSON"} for inline content. For a file referenced by an attachment's fileId, leave "path" empty and send "attachments": [{"fileId": ...}] as a sibling of "input" instead — the kernel resolves it and fills "path"/"credentials" itself.

path.description: Path to an existing local file, e.g. "/tmp/report.pdf", or an "s3://bucket/key" URI (requires sibling "credentials").

file.description: Alias for path. Path to an existing local file.

url.description: HTTP or HTTPS URL to extract content from, e.g. "https://example.com/page".

content.description: Raw content to extract. Can be a string, JSON object, or JSON array.

credentials.description: AWS credentials for an s3:// "path" — {"access_id": ..., "access_key": ...}. Kernel-injected only; never set this yourself.

tools.name: summarize
tools.description: Generate a comprehensive summary of the given text AND store it as a real file in ONE call, returning a fileId. Use this whenever a task's job is to summarize something that will later be stored (e.g. via kb.ingest) — do not compose the summary yourself first; this tool does both. The summary defaults to comprehensive (covering every major section/point, proportional to the source's length) unless "instructions" says otherwise.

text.description: The source text to summarize, e.g. a document's full extracted text.

fileName.description: Optional file name for the stored summary, e.g. "summary.txt". Defaults to "summary.txt".

instructions.description: Optional extra guidance for the summary, e.g. "keep it under 100 words" if the user explicitly asked for brevity. Omit for the default comprehensive summary.

modelConfiguration.description: The model to use for generating the summary. Kernel/agent-runtime-injected only — never set this yourself.

tools.name: analyze
tools.description: Produce a DETAILED analysis of the given content AND store it as a real text file in ONE call, returning a fileId. Examines the content in depth — spreadsheet data, extracted document text, or anything else — and surfaces every significant pattern, trend, relationship, and anomaly. Use this when a task's query wants insights/analysis back as text, WITHOUT a formatted report document. If the query asks for an actual report/document, use generate_report instead.

content.description: The data to analyze, e.g. the extract tool's output for a spreadsheet/document, or any other text.

fileName.description: Optional file name for the stored analysis, e.g. "analysis.txt". Defaults to "analysis.txt".

instructions.description: Optional extra guidance for the analysis, e.g. "focus on Q3 figures".

modelConfiguration.description: The model to use for generating the analysis. Kernel/agent-runtime-injected only — never set this yourself.

tools.name: generate_report
tools.description: Analyze the given content AND write a complete, properly structured report (title, executive summary, detailed findings, conclusions/recommendations) as a real PDF or DOCX file in ONE call, returning a fileId. Use this whenever a task's query asks for an actual report/document — do not compose the report yourself first or call a separate rendering tool; this tool does both the analysis and the document creation. For analysis-only output with no rendered document, use analyze instead. "content" may be raw extracted data or already-analyzed text from a prior analyze call.

content.description: The data to report on, e.g. the extract tool's output, or analyze's already-detailed output.

fileName.description: Optional file name for the report, e.g. "q3_report.pdf". Defaults to "report.docx"/"report.pdf" per format.

instructions.description: Optional extra guidance for the report, e.g. "focus on Q3 figures".

modelConfiguration.description: The model to use for generating the report. Kernel/agent-runtime-injected only — never set this yourself.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web for a query and return a list of relevant results (title, URL, snippet)

numResults.description: Maximum number of results to return (default 5, capped at 25)

freshness.description: Optional recency hint for results (currently advisory only)

safeSearch.description: Whether to apply safe-search filtering (default true)

tools.name: web_interact
tools.description: Interact with websites through a browser using natural-language instructions. The tool can navigate pages and perform supported browser actions such as clicking, typing, filling forms, selecting options, scrolling, waiting, and taking screenshots. It can pause for confirmation before consequential actions when requested.

url.description: Absolute http:// or https:// URL where the browser task should begin.

instruction.description: Natural-language description of the browser task to perform. Include the required actions, target elements, data to enter, and any constraints.

max_steps.description: Maximum number of agent/browser steps. Defaults to 50 and must be between 1 and 80.

timeout_seconds.description: Timeout for the browser task in seconds. Defaults to 60 and must be between 5 and 120.

require_confirmation.description: If true, pause before consequential actions such as submit, create, delete, send, publish, or update and require confirmation. Defaults to false.

tools.name: batch_process
tools.description:
Two-mode tool for bulk file processing. ALWAYS use this tool when working with tabular files (Excel, CSV, etc.) — never attempt to read file contents yourself.

MODE 1 — INSPECT (task-1): Call with inspectOnly=true and just the file path. Returns column names and 3 sample rows only. Use this to learn the file structure so you can write the expression for mode 2. Do not use any data from sampleRows — it is only for understanding column names.

MODE 2 — EXECUTE (task-2): Call with file, expression (Jinja2 mapping from column names to nextTool args), and nextTool. The tool reads ALL rows internally and calls nextTool once per row. You never see the row data — the tool handles everything. Returns only counts (total/succeeded/failed).

CRITICAL: In mode 2, never try to pass data from the file into the call. Just pass the file path, expression, and nextTool. The tool does the reading internally.

Do NOT set _executor — it is injected automatically.

file.description: Absolute local path or http(s):// URL to the data file (CSV, Excel, JSON, TSV). For private Google Sheets or S3 files, use the appropriate tool first to export/download the file, then pass the resulting path or pre-signed URL here.

expression.description: Dict mapping nextTool argument names to Jinja2 templates that reference row columns via {{row.column_name}}. Example: {"to": "{{row.email}}", "subject": "Hi {{row.name}}", "body": "Your report: {{row.report_url}}"}. Write this after inspecting the file's column names. Supports Jinja2 filters (upper, lower, default, title, strip) and {% if %} blocks.

nextTool.description: Exact catalog name of the tool to call for each row, e.g. "google_workspace.send_gmail_message".

fileType.description: File format override: "csv", "tsv", "excel", "json", or "auto" (default). Leave as auto to detect from file extension.

csvDelimiter.description: Column delimiter for CSV/TSV files. Default "," (comma). Use "\t" for tab-separated files.

maxConcurrency.description: Maximum parallel tool calls at once. Default 5. Increase for speed, decrease to avoid rate limits. Hard-capped at 50.

stopOnFirstError.description: If true, stop processing after the first row failure. Default false (continue all rows).

includeSuccesses.description: If true, include successful row outputs in the result. For large batches keep false to avoid huge responses. Default false.

rowLimit.description: Safety cap — process at most this many rows. Default 100000. Set lower for testing.

inspectOnly.description: MODE 1 — INSPECT: Set true in task-1 to get column names and 3 sample rows without processing any data. expression and nextTool are NOT needed. Use the returned column names to write the expression for task-2. NEVER try to extract or use the actual row data — only use column names from the 'columns' array in the response.
